page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server built on the AWS Nitro system architecture. The platform features an Intel x86_64 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources include 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio aligned with compute-focused execution rather than large in-memory footprints.

The server does not include integrated local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached volumes for persistent data and scratch space. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 67 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput data transfer between clustered nodes and storage services. The instance includes no GPU accelerators and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Resource allocation on c8ib.16xlarge emphasizes raw CPU clock speed and network bandwidth over memory density and local storage. This profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-constrained tasks that saturate execution cores without exceeding memory thresholds. The configuration is suited for distributed compute clusters, batch processing, algorithmic processing, compilation workloads, and network-intensive backend services.
